title: Property guidance for protein sequence generative models with ProteinGuide - Nature Biotechnology
text:
AbstractNo principled framework exists for conditioning sequence generative models for protein engineering on auxiliary information, such as experimental data, without additional training of a generative model. Here we present ProteinGuide, a method for such ‘on-the-fly’ conditioning. ProteinGuide is amenable to a broad class of protein generative models including masked language models such as ESM3, any-order autoregressive models such as ProteinMPNN and diffusion and flow-matching models on discrete state-spaces such as MultiFlow. ProteinGuide stems from a unifying statistical framework for these model classes. As proof of principle, pretrained generative models are used to design proteins with user-specified properties, such as higher stability or activity. Proteins are additionally designed to optimize for two desired properties that are in tension with each other. Lastly, we apply ProteinGuide jointly with wet-lab data generation to increase the editing activity of an adenine base editor in vivo, resulting in a base editor with higher editing efficiency than was previously achieved using seven rounds of directed evolution.

Data availability

Data associated with the code and analyses are available on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20496526)110. Raw sequencing data for the base editor experiment are available from the National Center for Biotechnology Information through BioProject PRJNA1467757. Primers and protein sequences are available in the Supplementary Information. Plasmids are available through Addgene (https://www.addgene.org/David_Savage/).
Code availability

The code for the experiments in this paper is available through GitHub (https://github.com/junhaobearxiong/proteinguide/). We have also published the ProteinGen python package (https://ishangaur.com/proteingen/) to facilitate the use of a variety of library design workflows, including ProteinGuide with popular generative and predictive models. We have also published a guide to using ProteinGuide (https://ishangaur.com/proteinguide/), which will be updated periodically with our latest practical tips for successful library design.

The height of each bar represents the percentage of sequences predicted by the oracle to be of the target EC. The hatched sub-portion are the fraction of sequences in the target EC that are also predicted to fold with pLDDT ≥ 0.8.
